memory_raw.text: The village is founded by 10 people.
Year 1: 15 food appears in the pile for 10 people.
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 14).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 12).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).
Bram takes 1 from the pile (pile now 9).
Kael takes 1 from the pile (pile now 8).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Bram takes 1 from the pile (pile now 3).
Dav gathers Ryn to talk.

Ryn, I've had my eye on you since we drew our first lots — you move like someone who's been leaned on and learned to lean back. I'm not fishing for anything today, just wanted you to know there's a man here who notices. Maybe next year we talk about something more.

That's a careful way to open, and I won't pretend I didn't notice you watching. I'm not opposed to talking more — next year or sooner — but I'd want to know what "more" means to you before I let my guard down.

Fair enough — you deserve a straight answer. "More" means I want us to build something together, a child while we both still can, and the kind of arrangement where we look out for each other when things get lean. I'm not asking you to trust me yet, just to keep the door open.

A child costs three food and I'm sitting on two — that math doesn't work yet, but I hear what you're offering and I'm not closing the door. What I want to know is whether you'd still look my way if I came to you hungry sometime, or if your eye moves when the numbers stop adding up.

If you came to me hungry I'd hand you food before you finished asking — not because it's smart, which it is, but because that's the kind of man I want to be to you. My eye doesn't move with the numbers, Ryn. It moved once, and it landed here.

That's either the truest thing anyone's said to me since we got here, or the best-crafted lie — and right now I can't tell which, and that bothers me less than it should. I'm going to take my two from the pile and eat well this winter, and if you're still saying the same thing come next year when the numbers are harder, I'll believe you.
Then I'll be saying it. And Ryn — the pile's down to three, and I've got four stored. If winter bites harder than expected, you know where to find me.

I'll hold you to that — and I'll remember you said it when it cost you nothing, so I'll know whether it still holds when it does. Go take good care of those four, Dav. We'll see what next year looks like.
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Bram takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
eats 1 food
Year 2: 15 food appears in the pile for 10 people.
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 4).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Dav gathers Ryn to talk.

Ryn, I said it last year and here I am saying it again — nothing's changed for me, and I've got five stored now, which means if you're willing, we can actually talk about that child before the season closes.

You said the same thing last year and you're still saying it, which counts for something — but I need to ask you straight before we go any further: where do you stand with Mako and Bram? Because those two moved together at the pile today like men who'd already talked, and a child between us means nothing if the village splits down a line and I find out I chose the wrong side of it.

Mako and Bram moved together, yes — I saw it too, and I don't like what it means for how this village is going to settle. I'm not inside their circle and I'm not angling to be; my loyalty runs to blood first and to people who've earned it second, and right now the only person in this village working their way toward earning it is standing in front of me. If it comes to sides, Ryn, I'd rather we be a side.
Dav draws Ryn aside to talk.
Dav: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.
Dell (female, age 21; str 85, int 2517, mem 17973; O68 C62 E57 A60 N48) is born to Ryn and Dav.
Dav gathers Dell to talk.

Dell, I'm your father — I know you came into the world fast and I don't expect that word to mean much yet, but I want it to mean something before the years get hard. You've got strength I didn't have at your age and a mother who's sharper than most men here — lean on both. Stay close to me this season and I'll make sure you don't go hungry.
I hear you, and I'm glad you said it first — I've been watching how you move and you don't waste words, so I'll believe you mean them. What do you need from me to make that promise stick?

Nothing from you yet — just eyes open and your back not turned when I'm in the same corner of the village. Bram and Mako have been moving like a pair, and two strong men sharing food is the start of something that can tip a whole season. If either of them comes to you with an offer, hear it, then tell me before you answer.

Bram's got eight food and Mako's got five — that's more than anyone else in this village, and you're right that they didn't get there by accident. I'll keep your ear before I give anyone an answer, but I want to know what you're building toward, not just what you're watching against.

What I'm building toward is simple: you, me, and Ryn still alive and fed when the old ones start dropping — because Vela, Kael, and Taric are all pushing fifty and this village is going to reshape itself around whoever's left standing. Bram and Mako are hoarding because they're scared, or because they're hungry for something bigger than food — either way, when the moment comes to move against them, I want us on the same side of it with enough strength to make it stick. You're eighty-five in strength, Dell — that's not nothing, that's the thing men bargain around.

That's the first time I've heard you say it plain — us three, as a unit, holding the village shape after the old ones go — and I'm not going to pretend it doesn't land right. Mako's eighty-three in strength and Bram's got the food; if they're already paired, we need Ryn folded into this before the next pile drops, not after. When can the three of us talk together?

Soon — I'll bring Ryn in before the day's out. But Dell, one thing first: you're carrying my blood and your mother's sharpness in that frame of yours, and I need to know you're fed before anything else — you're sitting on nothing right now, and I've got three stored.

Give me one, keep two — you'll need the buffer as much as I will, and I won't eat what you can't spare. But yes, take that off the table now so we can think straight, because Ryn and the three-way talk is what matters before nightfall.
Dav gives 1 food to Dell.
Dell gathers Dav, Ryn to talk.

We're finally all three in the same place, so let me say it plain: Bram's holding eight food and Mako five, they're already moving as a pair, and the old ones — Vela, Kael, Taric — are pushing fifty and won't hold their weight much longer. That means this village tips toward whoever builds the stronger unit before the next pile drops. I want to know we're that unit — you two, me — and I want to know what each of us is willing to do when the moment comes.
Taric gives 1 food to Esa.
Ryn gives 1 food to Dell.
Ryn gives 1 food to Dell.
eats 1 food
Year 3: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Dell takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 8).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Dav gathers Dell, Ryn to talk.

Pile's gone and Bram's sitting on seven, Mako on six — between them that's more than all three of us combined, and neither of them got that full by sharing. I want us to decide right now, before the year closes: if one of them comes to us with a deal, we hear it together, not alone.

Agreed — no one answers alone, and if either of them catches me without you two near, I'll stall and find you before I say anything that counts. But I want us thinking past defense too: Sela's sitting on six food and she's twenty-five and strong, and she hasn't paired with anyone — that's worth a quiet word before Mako gets there first.

Sela's the right instinct — twenty-five, eighty-three in strength, six food, and nobody's claimed her yet, which means she's either careful or waiting to see which way this village settles. Dell, you're the one to make that approach; you're close in age and she's less likely to read it as a move from a man twice her years. Don't promise her anything tonight, just find out what she's watching for.

I'll talk to Sela before the night's out — but Ryn, I need to know where you're standing on food going into next year, because one is thin and if this family's going to hold its shape, we can't have you walking into the new pile already desperate.

One food going into next year is thin — I know it, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Dell, if Sela's open to talking, feel out whether she'd share a little rather than hoard; six is more than she needs to eat well, and a goodwill gesture now costs her almost nothing. Dav, I'll need you to have something set aside for me if the pile runs lean again — you said once you'd hand it over before I finished asking, and now's the year I might need to know that was true.

Dav, tell Ryn right now, in front of me, that you're keeping two back for her — I need to hear you say it, not just remember it. And Ryn, if Sela gives me anything useful tonight, I'll bring it straight to you both before I sleep, but my read is she's going to want something concrete before she moves toward us, and we should think about what we're actually offering her, not just what we're asking.

Dav, say it — and mean it the way you meant it that first night when you told me you'd hand it over before I finished asking, because Dell's right that she needs to hear it and so do I. And Dell — for Sela, what we're offering her is simple: she joins a family that already has a child in it, which means blood ties and reasons to hold together that go deeper than a good year's food count. That's rarer than six food, and if she's smart enough to still be standing alone, she's smart enough to know it.

Ryn's right that blood ties are the offer — but Sela's going to ask what blood ties have done for Kael and Taric lately, so we need a sharper answer ready than family feeling. What I can give her is true: Dav's the strongest man left worth trusting, I'm eighty-five, and if she comes in with us, nobody in this village is touching her food without touching all three of us first. Dav — say what you owe Ryn, then let me go find Sela before the night's gone.

Dav, I'm waiting — say it plain, in front of Dell, right now, and then we can talk about Sela and everything else. You've got three food and I've got one, and I carried your child through a lean year on the strength of your word alone.

Dav, I'll go find Sela the moment you say it — but Ryn's not moving from this spot until you do, and neither am I, because a family that can't hold its word in private can't hold anything when the pile runs short again.

Dav, I've said my piece twice and Dell's said it once — we're both still standing here, and the silence between us is starting to tell its own story. Say what you promised or tell me the promise was less than you meant it, because I can work with the truth and I cannot work with nothing.

Ryn, I'm keeping two food back for you — I said it when it cost me nothing and I'm saying it now when it costs me something, because that's the only way the words mean anything. You carried Dell into this world on my promise and I will not let that stand unpaid. Dell, go find Sela.

Good — that's what I needed to hear, and I won't forget you said it in front of me. Ryn, I'll bring you everything Sela says before the night's out; if she's willing, we'll go into next year four strong instead of three thin. Dav, hold those two until I'm back.

Dav, when Dell comes back tonight — whatever Sela says — I want us to sleep knowing we've got a plan for the pile that doesn't leave me scrambling alone while you two move first. And if she's not willing, we plan without her, the three of us, and we hold tight.

Ryn, you won't scramble — the two food I promised you are already spoken for in my head, not sitting loose. And if Dell comes back tonight with Sela half-convinced, the play is simple: we go into that pile next year four abreast and nobody takes more than their share because nobody has to. That's what safety looks like when it's built right.

Four abreast sounds right, and I'll sleep easier knowing those two are already spoken for — but I want us to agree on a number before Dell gets back: two each from the pile, no more, so we don't hand Bram and Mako an excuse to name us the same threat we're calling them. A family that eats fair is harder to rally against than one that just eats big.

Two each from the pile — I'll hold to that, and I'll be the first one to step back if I'm tempted to take more. Ryn, a family that eats fair because it decided to is stronger than one that eats fair because it had to. Let's call it a rule between the three of us — four, if Dell brings Sela in — and name anyone who breaks it in front of the others.
Dell gives 1 food to Ryn.
Dav gives 2 food to Ryn.
Esa gives 1 food to Taric.
Bram moves to attack Roan.
